analysis.title: Bond Vigilantes Battle 'Bad News' Bulls; Big-Tech Bid Hides Ugly Equity Reality
key_insights: Oil, stocks and bonds broke out of the 'Iran War regime' this week: oil up, stocks flat, bonds down. Index moves hid a lot of damage underneath.
September payrolls rose 29,000 against a consensus of 84,000. August was revised down to 133,000, July went negative, and unemployment rose to 4.2%, mostly from labor-force re-entrants.
Futures-implied odds of an October Fed hike fell to 15% from almost 75% a week earlier. A December hike is still priced at about 85%, so the week delivered a postponement rather than a pivot.

The Fed raised rates a quarter point last month. Jefferson said colleagues need to reach their own judgment, which may take more time, and Williams also argued against blindly following through in October.

The 10Y yield rose a fourth straight day to 5.33% on Thursday, its highest since April 2002, with the 30Y at 5.67% and the 2Y at 4.91%. By Friday morning the 10Y was 5.18%, the 30Y 5.57% and the 2Y 4.73%. The curve steepened sharply on the week.
Core PCE printed 3.0% against a 3.3% forecast, but the undershoot owed much to methodological changes. Kashkari said it changed little for him, and the bond bid faded within hours.

ISM manufacturing showed new orders accelerating and cost pressures building, with prices paid rising from 71.1 to 77.9. Goldman's Privorotsky reads this as reacceleration into a supply constraint, not a stagflation signal, which means stickier goods inflation and less room for rates to fall.
CTA positioning in bonds was extremely short, which amplified the payrolls-day move.

Trump rejected Tehran's proposal to end the war, sent 9,000 additional troops, and said large-scale strikes could resume after the midterms. The rial hit 2,584,650 per dollar on Oct 1, down 98.6% over ten years.
Brent held above $100 and reached about $102 late Friday. Chinese refiners suspended fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and tanker attacks escalated.

G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel stocks. Bloomberg's Frank Monkam notes G7 crude reserves are near multi-decade lows, so releases imply later replenishment, and fading SPR releases has generally been a viable strategy.

Goldman's Privorotsky says alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers are getting meaningful barrels out. The durable consequence looks like a shipping cost and risk premium rather than lost barrels.

The French 10Y OAT yield rose to about 4.92-4.95%, its highest in roughly two decades, and the spread over Bunds passed 140bps, the widest since 2012. German yields fell while French yields rose, pointing to French fiscal and political risk, including a record EUR340 billion of issuance next year.
Italian BTPs were dragged in for the first time this episode. Privorotsky says that if BTPs move with OATs, the market is pricing European sovereign risk rather than French fiscal risk alone.
Deutsche Bank observes that financial stress is doing part of the ECB's tightening and may limit how far the ECB can go. The ECB deposit rate is 2.50% with further hikes priced through 2027.
The Bloomberg dollar index rose for a third straight week and broke the range it has held for 18 months. USD/JPY stalled near 158 and EUR/JPY fell to a ten-month low.
NDX was the only major US index to close green on the week. Dow was the biggest loser, and RTY and SPX were modest losers. Tech outperformed and financials lagged.

Market breadth is weak: new lows outpace new highs, fewer than half of S&P 500 members trade above their 200-day averages, and equal-weight indices underperform. Hartnett calls the market 'long artificial intelligence and short everything else'.

Accenture rose 21% on results and its fiscal 2027 outlook, Synopsys rose 12% on an Amazon cloud agreement and an OpenAI partnership, and Nike is down more than 40% on the year. NVDA hit a record high on its way to a $6 trillion market cap. Optical networking soared while NeoClouds lagged on credit concerns.

US high-yield spreads widened about 39bps on the week to around 312bps. CCC spreads reached 1,007bps, the first time above 1,000bps since March 2023. A $515 billion block of B-minus bonds and loans carries substantial loss risk.
Oracle's 5Y CDS hit a record of about 227bps and its 2056 bonds yield above 8%. Hyperscaler credit spreads remain wide relative to the equity market's view of their risk.

Gold stalled at the week's lows, with $4,200 described as the line in the sand. Physical buying continues: Silver Eagle sales doubled and the Bank of Korea is buying gold for the first time since 2013.

Bitcoin topped $87,000, its highest since September 23, then gave back gains as real rates spiked. US spot ETFs absorbed about $3 billion in a nine-session streak that broke Wednesday and resumed Thursday.

Global equity funds took in $34.76 billion in the week through Sept 30, after about $44 billion the prior week. Technology funds lost $2.63 billion, financials gained $1.13 billion, high yield lost $2.29 billion, energy funds lost $559 million, and money-market funds saw $116.5 billion of redemptions, the largest since April.

risk_factors: Bond market pushing yields higher on AI supply and fiscal concerns while AI-heavy equities assume earnings can outrun the cost of capital.
Credit contagion from CCC and B-minus debt, with a $515 billion block at risk as debt comes due.
Hyperscaler and AI-capex leverage, including Oracle's record CDS.
European sovereign stress spreading from France to Italy, with limited ECB room to respond.
Dollar strength and a 5% Treasury yield tightening global financial conditions.
Oil above $100 with tanker attacks and a narrowing window for a diplomatic off-ramp.
Diesel as a second-order inflation channel.
Narrow equity breadth, with the index dependent on a few AI names.
vol_and_positioning: CTA positioning in bonds was extremely short going into payrolls.
Goldman's Privorotsky says rates vol blew out while the S&P largely ignored it.
Fewer than half of S&P 500 members trade above their 200-day averages, and new lows outpace new highs.
Momentum rebounded sharply, and Mag7 outperformed the S&P 493, so equal-weight indices underperformed.
Hartnett describes the market as 'long artificial intelligence and short everything else'.
Global money-market funds saw $116.5 billion of redemptions, the largest weekly withdrawal since April.
Bloomberg's Monkam notes that fading SPR releases has generally been a viable alpha-generating strategy.
geopolitical: Trump rejected Tehran's proposal to end the war, said Iran must sign a deal or cease to exist, and sent 9,000 additional troops, with reports a further carrier group could follow.
Trump linked Tehran to Wednesday's attempted hijacking of an Israel-bound plane and told Time that large-scale strikes could resume after the midterms.
Iranian officials say the two sides differ mainly on the implementation timeline.
The Iranian rial hit 2,584,650 per dollar on Oct 1, having lost 98.6% of its value over ten years. The war began Feb 28 at a rate of about 1.65M.
Chinese refiners suspended fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau.
Tanker attacks escalated through the week, and a report of renewed hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis caused volatility Friday.
An AP-NORC poll found 69% of Americans say the war has not been worth fighting and 17% approve of Trump's handling of the cost of living, with the midterms weeks away.
France faces fiscal and political stress ahead of a presidential election, with a budget calling for a record EUR340 billion of issuance next year.
G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel stocks to address Trump's threatened US ban on diesel exports.

tension_points.bull_case: AI earnings and capex keep supporting the index, and NDX was the only major index to close green. NVDA hit a record and investors keep buying equities.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10Y at 5.33% and tightening financial conditions pull capital from equities. Breadth is poor, credit is cracking, and the bond market has become the speed limit for AI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit stress spreading beyond CCCs, such as high-yield spreads widening well past 312bps, or hyperscaler credit stress showing up in equity prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Weak payrolls and dovish comments from Jefferson and Williams cut October hike odds to 15%.
tension_points.bear_case: A December hike is still priced at about 85%, and ISM prices paid at 77.9 point to sticky inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot data print before the next meeting that revives October hike odds.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical routes are adapting and alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers are moving meaningful barrels. Crude flows are said to be normalizing.
tension_points.bear_case: Shipping costs and insurance remain extreme, G7 reserves are near multi-decade lows, and the SPR release does not fix structural supply problems.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credible threat to Hormuz removed, or a signed deal with Iran.
